summary_en: Systematic review of 36 articles (2021-2025) on data-driven learning analytics and machine learning in higher education. Finds a disconnect between the models used and the available educational data and a lack of psychopedagogical and data governance frameworks.

title: Automated Mental Health Evaluation From Text using ML And NLP
screening_reason: Population: professionals and students
summary_en: Proposes a framework for predicting mental health issues from text using NLP and XGBoost, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes and Logistic Regression. No data or results are reported.

title: Facial Expression-Based Mental Health Prediction in Remote Learning
summary_en: Trains machine learning models on facial action unit features extracted with OpenFace from 349 remote-learning videos of 76 college students to predict mental health states. Decision Tree performs best for depression (AUC 0.594), with AU09, AU25 and AU07 as the most important features.

title: Analyzing Sensitive Factors Affecting Online Academic Performance in the New Normal: A Machine Learning Perspective
screening_reason: Main outcome is online academic performance
summary_en: Examines factors affecting online academic performance using survey responses from 978 junior and senior high school students in the Philippines, Boruta feature selection, an MLP neural network and sensitivity analysis. The MLP reaches 0.932 accuracy, and motivation and mental well-being are the most sensitive factors.

title: Detection and Analysis of Stress-Related Posts in Reddit’s Acamedic Communities
best_result: Bag of Words + Logistic Regression accuracy 77.78%, F1 0.79
summary_en: Detects stress in posts from Reddit academic communities using NLP and classifiers trained on the Dreaddit dataset, validated on 100 manually annotated academic posts (72% accuracy). The overall stress level in academic texts is 29%, with professors' communities more stressed than bachelor's, graduate and PhD student communities.

title: A Machine Learning-Based Approach to Cognitive Behavioural Therapy for Adolescents' Academics: A Systematic Review
screening_reason: Focus on academic performance; conceptual review
summary_en: Reviews how machine learning could extend cognitive behavioral therapy to address adolescents' academic challenges through personalized interventions. No included studies, data or results are reported.

title: Enhancing Student Management Through Hybrid Machine Learning and Rough Set Models: A Framework for Positive Learning Environments
screening_reason: Outcome is academic outcomes; well-being only mentioned
summary_en: Presents a hybrid framework combining machine learning classifiers and rough set rules to identify at-risk students from academic, behavioral and engagement data in the OULAD dataset. It reaches 97.85% accuracy, about 15% above conventional methods.

title: Analyzing Factors of Mental Health Problems among Malaysian University Students using Clustering Analysis
summary_en: Identifies factors of mental health problems in 635 Malaysian university students by relating DASS-21 scores to WHOQOL facets with Two-step and k-means clustering. Students with severe scores rate lowest on study, self-esteem, memory and positive feelings.

title: AI-Powered Mental Health Screening and Support for Homeless Children
screening_reason: Population: homeless children, not framed as students
summary_en: Develops an SVM model that screens the mental health status of homeless children from Pediatric Symptom Checklist responses for use by orphanage caretakers. The model achieves 90% accuracy.

title: Predictive Tool for Peer Support and Mental Health Improvement with Speech Emotion State Classification for University Students
summary_en: Proposes a peer support application with a predictive tool that classifies speech emotion states of university students using convolutional neural networks to monitor mental health progress. No data or results are reported.

title: Smart Detection and Proactive Prevention of Student Depression: A DeepLearning Approach
summary_en: Proposes a system that detects student depression from facial expressions (CNN) and voice patterns, trained on a collected student face and audio dataset. It reports high accuracy without quantifying it.

title: Precision Wellness in Learning: IoT's Role in Optimizing Student Well-being using Cloud Computing
summary_en: Proposes an IoT and cloud system using wearables (heart rate, sleep, activity, stress) to track students' emotional and physical health in classrooms and link it to academic achievement with machine learning. No data or results are reported.

title: Design and Implementation of a Dynamic Early Warning Algorithm for Mental Health Risks Driven by Big Data
summary_en: Designs a dynamic mental health early warning algorithm based on improved XGBoost with multi-source data fusion, tested on psychological, behavioral and academic data from 12,785 college students. It achieves 86% accuracy and AUC 0.91, outperforming SVM and RNN, with a two-week warning lead time.

title: Improving mental health literacy using AI: A Scoping Review
screening_reason: Population: patients/adults, not students
summary_en: Scoping review of eight articles on how AI has been used to improve mental health literacy in the United States. AI is used through role-play simulations, chatbots and LLMs, and machine and deep learning, mainly for depression, suicide prevention, ADHD and PTSD.

title: Mental Health Monitoring in Higher Education Using Machine Learning and Computer Vision
summary_en: Proposes a multimodal framework for detecting depressive symptoms in university students and staff that fuses surveys, video interviews and social media text with NLP, computer vision, and deep and traditional machine learning. Strong predictive performance is claimed without metrics.

title: Cognitive Framework for Predicting Students' Anxiety Levels Using Optimized Feed Forward Networks
summary_en: Proposes a Pelican-optimized feed-forward network to classify students' anxiety levels using Kaggle anxiety datasets, compared with other machine learning models. It reaches 0.983 accuracy and 0.982 F1 with 50% shorter model building time.

title: Machine Learning Based Student Mental Health Predictor
summary_en: Proposes a machine learning system that analyzes psychological and academic data to identify students at mental health risk. No algorithms, data details or results are reported.

title: Predicting School Dropout and Simulating Educational Scenarios in Colombia Using Machine Learning
screening_reason: Not about mental health; school dropout
summary_en: Develops a platform that predicts school dropout risk in Colombia from national and local historical data using decision trees, SVM and neural networks, with a policy simulation module. The neural network achieves over 85% accuracy.

title: Computing cluster and artificial intelligence in the analysis and application of college students' physical exercise behavior
screening_reason: Not about mental health; computing cluster for physical exercise
summary_en: Studies load balancing in computing clusters and an AI training model applied to college students' physical exercise. Results are reported only as efficient.

title: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Depression in Bangladeshi University Students
summary_en: Compares five models (Logistic Regression, KNN, Random Forest, Decision Tree, CNN) to predict depression in 927 Bangladeshi undergraduates assessed with a Bangla DASS-21. CNN achieves the highest accuracy (91%), followed by Random Forest (85%).

title: Exploring the Intersection of Artificial Intelligence and Mental Health: Data-Driven Approaches
screening_reason: Vague abstract; population includes various groups
summary_en: Presents a Python-based data analysis of factors affecting mental health, targeting groups such as college students. Data, models and results are not described.

title: A Multimodal Fusion Network for Student Emotion Recognition Based on Transformer and Tensor Product
summary_en: Proposes a multimodal Transformer model fusing BERT text vectors and ViT image vectors through tensor products to classify students' psychological conditions. It reaches 93.65% accuracy, outperforming CLIP and ViLBERT; the dataset is not described.

title: Insights into Mental Health Challenges in Digital Education using Suitable Machine Learning Techniques
summary_en: Predicts students' mental health status in online learning from survey responses using numerous classifiers (Random Forest, SVM, KNN, gradient boosting, MLP, stacking, among others). Decision Tree performs best (75% accuracy, F-score 82.7%).

title: Machine Learning as A Tool for Predicting and Enhancing Student Motivation and Engagement
screening_reason: Outcome is motivation and engagement, not mental health; conceptual
summary_en: Discusses how machine learning and NLP can predict and enhance student motivation and engagement from demographic, behavioral and textual data. No data or results are reported.

title: Multi-Site Mild Traumatic Brain Injury Classification with Machine Learning and Harmonization
screening_reason: Not about students; traumatic brain injury neuroimaging
summary_en: Shows that harmonization of multi-site resting-state functional connectivity data should be integrated into machine learning classification of mild traumatic brain injury. No metrics are reported.

title: Assessing Social Media's Impact on Mental Health: A Gaussian Naive Bayes Approach
screening_reason: Does not address students
summary_en: Analyzes the impact of social media on mental health using a dataset of 481 records with correlation analysis, visualization and several models. Gaussian Naive Bayes yields the highest accuracy, and social media engagement is associated with negative mental well-being.

title: Mental Wellness ChatBot for Students Using NLP
summary_en: Proposes a mental well-being chatbot for students using NLP, sentiment analysis and keyword detection, with Spotify mood-based music recommendations and Twilio distress alerts. No data or metrics are reported.

title: Facial Emotion Recognition for Students Using Machine Learning
screening_reason: Abstract discusses only ethical concerns; no data or method
summary_en: Discusses privacy, discrimination and accuracy concerns of using machine learning for facial emotion recognition in students. No data, method or results are presented.

title: Personalizing Loneliness Detection Through Behavioral Grouping of Passive Sensing Data From College Students
summary_en: Detects loneliness in college students using smartphone passive sensing data from 41 students, unsupervised clustering into behavioral subgroups and group-specific classification models. Group-based models significantly improve accuracy over generalized models.

title: Classification of Stress in Students using Machine Learning Algorithms
summary_en: Predicts student stress levels from a Google Forms survey using the PSS-10 and SVM, KNN and Naive Bayes classifiers. SVM achieves the highest accuracy (95.32%).

title: EmoSupport: A Comparative Study for the Analysis of Mental Health of Undergraduate Students
summary_en: Compares Decision Trees, Naive Bayes, SVM and Random Forest for predicting anxiety, depression and stress levels of undergraduate students from questionnaire scores. No sample size or metrics are reported.

title: Predictive Modeling of Anxiety Levels in Bangladeshi University Students: A Voting-Based Approach with LIME and SHAP Explanations
summary_en: Predicts anxiety in university students in Bangladesh from a Google Form survey using a voting classifier built on the three best algorithms and 20 selected features, explained with LIME and SHAP. The voting classifier reaches 96% accuracy.

title: Analysis of Factors Affecting Digital Literacy: Technology Use and Student Engagement in Higher Education
screening_reason: Not about mental health; digital literacy
summary_en: Examines factors contributing to digital literacy and technology use among higher education students through semi-structured interviews and correlation analysis. No specific results are reported.

title: Machine Learning-Based Classification of Mental Health State Using the DASS-21 Profile
summary_en: Compares six machine learning models to classify depression, anxiety and stress from DASS-21 profiles using 2,602 records from the University of Phayao Counselling Center. The deep learning model performs best, with accuracy above 90% and AUC above 99%.

title: Early Identification of Suicide-Susceptible Students using Computational Techniques
summary_en: Proposes machine learning models to predict suicide risk levels (high, medium, low) in college students from data such as depression levels and discrimination experiences. No data or results are reported.

title: Multimodal Educational Data Fusion for Students’ Mental Health Detection
summary_en: Proposes CASTLE, a framework that fuses social life, academic performance and physical appearance data via representation learning (MOON network embedding), SMOTE and a deep neural network to detect university students' mental health problems. It reports promising performance against baselines without metrics.

title: Exploring Mental Well-Being Based on Daily Routine Patterns and on the Impact of Sleep Quality
screening_reason: Population not specified as students
summary_en: Examines the influence of routine regularity and sleep quality on mental well-being in 376 participants using machine learning classification. XGBoost achieves 88.20% accuracy, and routine regularity and 7-9 hours of sleep are the strongest predictors.

title: Sentiment-based Mental Health Monitoring System for Students using Hybrid ML and Transformer-based NLP
summary_en: Proposes a transformer-based sentiment analysis framework for student mental health monitoring from user-generated text. Multilingual BERT performs best; the dataset and metrics are not described.

title: Multi-dimensional Student Group Portrait Construction Based on Visualization System and Its Application in Class Meeting Assistance
screening_reason: Psychological status is only one dimension of student portraits for class management
summary_en: Proposes multi-dimensional student group portraits (academic performance, self-regulated learning, psychological status, social interaction) built with machine learning and a visualization system to assist university counselors in class meetings. No data or quantitative results are reported.

title: Predictions of College Students’ Mental Stress using Machine Learning Algorithms
summary_en: Predicts college students' mental stress around examinations and internet use from surveys at several institutions using Decision Tree, SVM, Naive Bayes and KNN. KNN achieves the highest accuracy (87.2%).

title: Leveraging Machine Learning to Personalize Learning and Reduce Close Book Examination Stress
screening_reason: Conceptual essay focused on personalized learning
summary_en: Discusses how machine learning-based personalized learning and formative assessment could reduce closed-book examination stress. No data, method or results are presented.

title: Artificial Intelligence’s Contribution To Mental Health Education
screening_reason: Does not address students; conceptual overview
summary_en: Reviews AI types that may support mental health education and describes an AI-based chatbot platform for identifying mental health factors. No data or results are reported.

title: Predicting Heart Rate Variability from Heart Rate and Step Count for University Student Weekdays
summary_en: Trains machine learning models to estimate heart rate variability from heart rate and step count using 201 hours of wearable data from 14 university students. Highest-stress periods are predicted with moderate performance (AUC 0.746).

title: Machine Learning Models based Mental Health Detection
summary_en: Screens mental disorders (mood, anxiety, depression, eating and sleep disorders) in students with supervised machine learning on SRQ-15 and SRQ-25 questionnaires. Algorithms and results are not reported.

title: Machine Learning Approach to Analyse the Mental Health and Predict Nomophobia
summary_en: Predicts nomophobia severity in 841 university students in Kosovo using Random Forest, descriptive statistics and Pearson correlation. Random Forest explains about 98% of the variance (R² 0.9773), and nomophobia correlates positively with anxiety, stress and depression.

title: Smart Learning with Stress Detection: Enhancing Online Education Through AI-Driven Question Answering and Emotional Well-Being Monitoring
summary_en: Proposes a smart learning system that combines automatic question generation (T5, BERT) with a facial emotion recognition module to monitor student stress in online learning. No data or results are reported.

title: Ensemble Machine Learning for Stress Level Detection in Thesis Students
best_result: Random Forest + Naive Bayes ensemble accuracy 99.57%
summary_en: Assesses ensemble machine learning for detecting stress in 501 thesis students from seven universities using a modified Student-Life Stress Inventory. The Random Forest and Naive Bayes ensemble reaches 99.57% accuracy, surpassing individual baselines.

title: Analysis and prediction of factors affecting student grades based on machine learning algorithms
screening_reason: Not about mental health; academic grades
summary_en: Clusters and predicts student grades using a UCI open dataset to identify factors related to academic performance. No metrics are reported.

title: Construction of a physical health monitoring platform for adolescents driven by big data
screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical health
summary_en: Builds a big data platform for monitoring adolescents' physical health with machine learning on 15 fitness indicators, piloted in five schools with over 15,000 students. Early warning accuracy reaches 92.3%.

title: Mind Matters: Harnessing Machine Learning to Predict Psychiatric Diagnoses in University Students with Real-World Data
summary_en: Predicts psychiatric diagnoses among undergraduates from demographic, lifestyle and psychometric survey data using various classifiers. The Multi-layer Perceptron is the most effective; sample size and metrics are not reported.

title: Early Detection of Student Depression Using Deep Learning Algorithms
summary_en: Proposes a system using CNN, LSTM and RNN to detect early-stage depression in students from standardized questionnaires and behavioral factors (mood, sleep, social interaction, school performance). No data size or results are reported.

title: Artificial Intelligence in International Students' Learning: A Bibliometric Analysis
screening_reason: Not about mental health; bibliometric analysis of AI in learning
summary_en: Bibliometric analysis of 185 Scopus publications on AI applications for international students' learning. Research output is growing and four thematic clusters are identified.

title: Toward Educational Sustainability: An AI System for Identifying and Preventing Student Dropout
screening_reason: Outcome is dropout, not mental health
summary_en: Develops a web application to identify dropout probability at SENA using socioeconomic variables, comparing decision trees, K-means and regression. The decision tree reaches 91% accuracy.

title: Studying the Effectiveness of Online College Education in India from Student Feedback
summary_en: Analyses factors affecting university students' mental health during the pandemic and online learning using data collected at the authors' university and clustering algorithms. DBSCAN yields 8 clusters with 2% noise and K-means 3 clusters, without predictive metrics.

title: Prediction of Students' Employment Prospect Based on GBDT Algorithm Model
screening_reason: Outcome is employment prospects, not mental health
summary_en: Predicts university students' employment prospects from career choice, salary and self-realisation indicators, comparing RF, SVM and GBDT. GBDT shows the best predictive ability.

title: Tree-Based Multiclass Learning Model for Physiological Stress Detection from Students Community
summary_en: Proposes a tree-based multi-label model (DT, RF, AdaBoost, XGBoost) to predict stress factors in students. Random Forest performs best with 90% accuracy; the abstract does not describe the data.

title: An Extensive Research of Women Distress Arising from Harassment Circumstances: Leveraging Data Analytics and Machine Learning Methodologies to Systematically Address the Psychological Distress and Apprehension through web app
screening_reason: Population is women experiencing harassment, not students
summary_en: Examines forms of harassment experienced by women and their mental health impact, mentioning machine learning algorithms and a web app. Data, method and results are not described.

title: Design and Development of College Counsellors Job Management System of College Counsellors Based on LLM
screening_reason: Focus is counsellor job management, not mental health
summary_en: Designs a job management system for college counsellors based on GPT-4 fine-tuned on academic records, counselling cases and psychological counselling manuals. It achieves 95.8% semantic matching accuracy and a 42% productivity gain in a trial across three universities.

title: A Federated Learning-Based Hybrid Model for Enhancing Student Engagement and Emotional Growth in Universities
summary_en: Proposes a federated hybrid CNN-BiLSTM model to analyse university students' engagement and emotional well-being from engagement logs and emotional expressions. It reaches 96.2% accuracy and outperforms centralised RF, SVM and CNN/BiLSTM baselines.

title: Enhanced Student Stress Prediction in Higher Education Using a TriBranch CNN Framework
summary_en: Presents a TriBranch CNN framework with PCA to predict college students' stress. The abstract reports that Fully CTBN reaches 93.29% accuracy versus CNN and FCN, without describing the data.

title: Depression Level Prediction For Students Using Machine Learning In The Context of Bangladesh
summary_en: Predicts depression level in students in Bangladesh using psychologist-selected factors and eight classifiers. SMO performs best; no metrics or sample size are reported.

title: Neural Deep Learning Models for Learning Analytics in a Digital Humanities Laboratory
screening_reason: Focus is learning analytics; emotions are an input
summary_en: Presents a deep learning architecture for a digital humanities laboratory that captures multimodal data and facial expressions to classify student emotions. It is a preliminary experiment without performance metrics.

title: Exploring the Impact of Financial Stress on Students’ Academic Performance: A Machine Learning Approach
summary_en: Models financial stress in 2,902 college students and its link to academic success using daily activities and wrist-sensor pulse data with J48, RF, Naive Bayes and KNN. The model reaches 85% training and 82% test accuracy.

title: A Survey on Predicting Depression Among Teachers and Students at Metropolitan University (Sylhet, Bangladesh) Using Machine Learning
screening_reason: Mixed population: students and non-students
summary_en: Detects depression among teachers and students of Metropolitan University (Sylhet) from 516 survey responses using logistic regression, decision trees and Gradient Boosting. It reports that causes of depression differ by sex, without performance metrics.

title: Forecasting the Academic Horizon: Machine Learning Models Unraveling the Complex Web of Student Well-being Determinants
summary_en: Predicts student well-being from personal attributes, academic performance and economic indicators with models ranging from logistic regression to ensembles. Tuned Gradient Boosting reaches 77.63% accuracy and Random Forest 77.29%.

title: The Transition From Centralized Machine Learning to Federated Learning for Mental Health in Education: A Survey of Current Methods and Future Directions
summary_en: Reviews machine learning studies on student mental health and federated learning applications in mental health. It proposes a research roadmap for privacy-preserving federated learning in educational settings.

title: A BI Approach for Student Engagement and Retention along with Cognitive Load Analysis for Educator
screening_reason: Focus is engagement, retention and cognitive load; mental health only an indicator
summary_en: Proposes a business intelligence framework combining attendance, performance, mental health indicators, demographics and feedback to monitor engagement and retention, plus cognitive load analysis. No quantitative metrics are reported.

title: EmbraceEase- Your Personal Oasis in Virtual Landscape
screening_reason: General population, not students
summary_en: Presents EmbraceEase, a web-based mental wellness chatbot that categorises users and generates personalised questions with AI and NLP to estimate illness level and suggest remedies. No data or evaluation are described.

title: Predictive Modeling of Student Academic Performance in External Examinations
screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance, not mental health
summary_en: Predicts students' GPA in external exams from internal scores, previous semester scores and attendance using several machine learning algorithms. No metrics are reported.

title: Service Chatbots and International Students: A Systematic Review
summary_en: Reviews research on difficulties faced by international students in the US and the effectiveness of AI-based chatbots for mental health support. The review method and findings are not detailed.

title: Bridging Precision and Transparency: XAI Models for Predicting Students Depression
summary_en: Proposes an interpretable depression prediction model for college students using machine learning with SHAP and LIME on conduct, school functioning and lifestyle variables. It claims accurate prediction without reporting metrics or data.

title: Automation of the psychological care process in university students using machine learning
summary_en: Implements an AI-based data analysis system to visualise university students' psychological test results and support psychologists' diagnosis. It reports faster and better-quality care without metrics.

title: Mobile Emotion Healthcare System Applying Sentiment analysis
screening_reason: Population not specified as students; evaluates technology acceptance
summary_en: Develops a mobile emotion healthcare system using machine learning and sentiment analysis and evaluates intention to use with HBM and TAM. Health consciousness, perceived usefulness, perceived ease of use and attitude significantly affect intention to use.

title: From Exploration to Explanation: Navigating Student Anxiety in Higher Education with AI
summary_en: Identifies drivers of anxiety in university students in a non-pandemic period using descriptive analysis and an XGBoost classifier on 194 features interpreted with SHAP. Academic impairment is the strongest predictor, followed by perceived need for help and racial trauma.

title: Machine Learning Based Prediction of Psychiatric Disorder
summary_en: Addresses the impact of COVID-19 on students' mental health through a binary classification model with neural networks for psychiatric disorders. Data and results are not described.

title: Automated Mental Stress Detection Among School Children Through Machine Learning Techniques
summary_en: Classifies stress (low, moderate, high) in school children using 980 records from the Student Stress Survey Questionnaire, comparing RF, DT, SVM, KNN and Gradient Boosting. SVM and RF achieve the highest accuracy.

title: Quantified Cross-Cultural Adaptability Model for Intelligent Grouping in Chinese Classroom
screening_reason: Focus is cross-cultural adaptation and classroom grouping
summary_en: Groups international students in China with K-means based on cultural novelty and psychological capital to build a cross-cultural adaptation model. No data or metrics are reported.

title: Context-Aware Mental Health Diagnostics Using Bi-LSTM in Higher Education: A Survey-Based Study in Sultanate of Oman
summary_en: Builds a Bi-LSTM model for early detection of anxiety and depression in undergraduate students in Oman using survey data with demographics, academic indicators and HADS responses. The pipeline is described without performance metrics.

title: ZJ-EduFormer: Predicting Supply Chain Student Stress Using Transformer
summary_en: Proposes ZJ-EduFormer, a Transformer model to predict stress in 2,000 supply chain management students from lifestyle features. It outperforms classical and deep baselines with R2 0.856 and a 26.1% RMSE reduction.

title: Deep Learning Integration and AI-Driven Support: A Comprehensive Student Platform for Emotion Detection, Psychological Assessment, and Career Guidance
summary_en: Presents a mental health platform for grade 11-12 students with emotion detection, GAD-7, SRQ-20 and PHQ-9 assessments, a chatbot and career guidance. No quantitative evaluation is reported.

title: Effects of Peer Monitoring on Student Stress Level of College Students Based on Multi-Layer Perceptron Approach
summary_en: Adapts the SSI-SM inventory for college students and predicts stress with normalisation, LDA and information-gain feature selection and an MLP. The MLP outperforms CNN and RNN, without numeric metrics.

title: An Interpretable Cross-Regional Prediction Study of University Students’ Mental Health Based on XGBoost and SHAP
summary_en: Develops a multi-task XGBoost framework predicting depression severity and perceived stress from university students' daily behavioural indicators, with cross-regional SHAP analyses. It outperforms logistic regression and Random Forest and reveals context-dependent behavioural patterns.

title: Health Recommendation Model for Student Drug Addiction Risk Using Automated Machine Learning and Optimized Feature Selection
summary_en: Proposes a health recommender system predicting drug addiction risk in students with AutoML (TPOT) and multi-objective feature selection (MOHHO). It outperforms RFE, mutual information and correlation-based selection, without reporting metrics or data.

title: Voice-Based Machine Learning Model for Depression Risk Prediction in Medical Students: A Review
summary_en: Systematic review (PRISMA, 2015-2025) of voice-based machine learning models for depression prediction in medical students. SVM, RF and CNN are most common and MFCC and prosodic features are relevant, but dataset heterogeneity limits generalisability.

title: AnxPred: A Hybrid CNN-SVM Model with XAI to Predict Anxiety among University Students
summary_en: Proposes AnxPred, a hybrid CNN-SVM model predicting anxiety (GAD-7) from 2,028 responses across 15 universities in Bangladesh. It achieves F1 99.134%, outperforming conventional models, and LIME shows it captures relevant academic stressors.

title: Research on the Application of Computer Big Data Technology in College Japanese Grammar Teaching
screening_reason: Not about mental health; Japanese grammar teaching
summary_en: Discusses the application of big data to college Japanese grammar teaching. No data, method or results are described.

title: Screening Students for Stress Using Fitbit Data
summary_en: Evaluates a Fitbit dataset for stress screening in college students using machine learning. Physiological data such as calories burned and sleep support screening with F1 up to 0.81.

title: Predictive Modeling of Anxiety Disorders Among Final-Year Students Using a Comparative Machine Learning Approach
summary_en: Compares RF, SVM and LSTM to predict anxiety disorders (HARS) in 151 final-year students with SMOTE. Random Forest performs best (accuracy 0.9032; ROC-AUC 0.9976).

title: Stressmonitoring System in a Mobile Application for Medical Science Students
summary_en: Develops a mobile app monitoring medical students' stress from Empatica E4 physiological data with standard and balanced Random Forest. They reach 91.18% and 88.57% accuracy; the system was trialled with two students during clinical shifts.

title: Smart Smartphones for Mental Health
summary_en: Predicts mental health status of 79 university students in Bangladesh from smartphone sensor data (GPS, power state, Bluetooth, accelerometer) collected with Beiwe, using three regressors. Random Forest performs best (RMSE 1.303; R2 0.425), with modest accuracy.

title: Protecting Student Mental Health with a Context-Aware Machine Learning Framework for Stress Monitoring
summary_en: Proposes a context-aware framework to classify student stress on two survey-based datasets using feature selection, PCA, six base classifiers and ensemble strategies. It achieves 93.09% with weighted voting (Student Stress Factors) and 99.53% with stacking (Stress and Well-being).

title: Depression Severity Prediction Among Higher Education Students Using Neural Network Model
summary_en: Classifies depression severity in higher education students from PHQ-9 responses and descriptive text using DNN, LSTM and hybrid models. LSTM achieves the highest precision (90%).

title: Helm: A Data-Driven Framework for Mitigating Digital Burnout Through Personalized Analytics on Student Wellbeing and Mobile Interaction
summary_en: Presents Helm, a platform to mitigate college students' digital burnout that combines daily journaling and mobile interaction data with sentiment analysis to measure stress and anxiety. No evaluation is reported.

title: Building and Using State-Anxiety-Oriented Graph for Student State Anxiety Assessment in Online Classroom Scenarios
summary_en: Builds a dataset of 3,701 video clips from 106 high school students in online classes and proposes a graph-based method with attention modules integrating course, event, academic and mental health information to assess state anxiety. It obtains MSE 0.1380 and MAE 0.2768.

title: Mental Health Detection Using EEG Signals
summary_en: Proposes a system combining portable EEG and questionnaires to classify the mental health of youths aged 16-25 as good or needing consultation, aimed at institutional monitoring of students. No results are reported.

title: AI-Based Prediction of Mental Health Using a Reduced DASS-21 Survey: A Case Study on KIIT University Students
summary_en: Evaluates a reduced 7-item DASS-21 among KIIT University students with MentalBERT, Random Forest and logistic regression under stratified cross-validation. Classification with the 7 items matches or exceeds the full DASS-21.

title: Using Machine Learning to Construct a Simplified Scale for Assessing Mental Status Among Undergraduates
summary_en: Simplifies screening scales (SBQ-R, PHQ-9, GAD-7, ISI) using data from 32,868 undergraduates at three Chinese universities, applying mRMR feature selection and four algorithms to 2,632 cases. The reduced scales preserve reliability and shorten assessment time.

title: Predicting Adolescent Mental Health from Social, Academic & Health Data
screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; adolescent population not clearly students
summary_en: Predicts adolescent mental health from personal, academic and text data, comparing structured models (LR, RF, XGBoost, LightGBM, CatBoost) and NLP models. Text-based models outperform structured-data models, without specific metrics.

title: Depression Prediction among Students using Machine Learning and Voting Ensembles: An Explainable AI Approach
summary_en: Predicts student depression on a Kaggle dataset of 27,901 records using XGBoost, CatBoost, LightGBM, HGB, RF and voting ensembles with XAI. CatBoost achieves the best AUC-ROC (0.9210).

title: Classification of Social Media Addiction in Students Using Machine Learning
summary_en: Classifies social media addiction stages (low, moderate, high) in students from demographic and behavioural attributes using LightGBM, J48 and DecisionStump. LightGBM reaches 98% accuracy; female students and those aged 19-21 show higher risk.

title: Predicting Student Depression Using Machine Learning: A Performance-Based Model Comparison
summary_en: Compares RF, SVM, neural networks and logistic regression to predict student depression on the Student Depression Dataset (academic, demographic and behavioural data). Random Forest performs best (accuracy 88.4%); GPA, behavioural markers and psychological tests are the main predictors.

title: Monitoring of Physiological Response Specific to Sleep Deprivation
screening_reason: Outcome is sleep deprivation, not mental health
summary_en: Detects physiological responses to sleep deprivation in 424 samples from 129 college students using ECG and accelerometry (35 features) and five classifiers. Gradient Boosting performs best with F1 73.09%.

title: Factors Affecting Mental Health of High School Students due to COVID-19: An Exploratory Study
summary_en: Assesses mental health and contributing factors in 158 high school students (10-19 years) during COVID-19 using an online survey, chi-square tests, path analysis and ML classifiers (LR, SVM, NB, AdaBoost, RF). AdaBoost scores highest (86%); online class difficulties, sleep disruption and prolonged device use are major factors.

title: Applying Deep Learning and Machine Learning for Detecting Gender Bias in Teaching Student Feedback: Toward a Gender-Bias-Free University
screening_reason: Outcome is gender bias in teaching evaluations, not student mental health
summary_en: Detects explicit gender bias in 960 Spanish student teaching-evaluation comments from the University of Bio-Bio using SVM, BETO and DistilBERT. BiLSTM-enhanced transformers reach macro F1 99%, above BETO (95%) and SVM (88%).

title: Predicting Psychological State of Students based on Physiological, Behavioral, and Environmental Attributes
summary_en: Predicts students' psychological states from physiological (HRV, skin response, brain activity), environmental, behavioural and demographic features using decision tree classifiers selected by IBM Watson. The best model, a Decision Tree, reaches only about 30% accuracy.

title: Early Detection and Intervention of Students’ Depression Risk Factors using Predictive Models: Insights and Implications

summary_en: Classifies suicidal behaviours in medical students from an expert-developed self-report questionnaire (688 instances, 342 features on socioeconomic status, substance use and trauma) using SVM and Random Forest. SVM achieves AUC 0.81 and Random Forest 0.80.

title: Machine Learning for Early Detection of Learning Disabilities in Primary School Students
screening_reason: Outcome is learning disabilities, not mental health
summary_en: Proposes a machine learning framework for early detection of learning disabilities in primary school students using academic records, behavioural observations and cognitive test results. It reports promising accuracy, precision and recall without specific values.

title: The Construction of Intelligent Homework System in Schools under the Concept of Wisdom Education
screening_reason: Not about mental health; intelligent homework system
summary_en: Proposes an intelligent homework system based on big data and an adaptive learning model to address challenges in post-pandemic online education. It does not address mental health.

title: A Novel Model for Student's Mental Health Monitoring Based on Hard and Soft Data Fusion
summary_en: Proposes a student mental health monitoring model fusing hard data (speech emotion recognition with CNN-LSTM to estimate depression probability) and soft data (psychologists' opinions modelled with Dempster-Shafer theory). No dataset or evaluation results are reported.

title: Prediction of Depression and Anxiety on University Students in Bangladesh Using Machine Learning
summary_en: Predicts four stages of depression and anxiety in university students in Bangladesh from text input using Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Random Forest, neural networks, KNN and a stacking model with LDA as meta-classifier, trained on over 10,800 (depression) and 14,500 (anxiety) records. The stacking model achieves 99% and 97% test accuracy.

title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Stress Levels in Students with Social Media Addiction
summary_en: Detects stress levels in students with social media addiction using preprocessed social media content, mRMR and chi-square feature selection, and an attention-based graph convolutional network. The model achieves 92.84% accuracy, outperforming Random Forest and standard GCN.

title: Psychological Profiling of Digital Dependency Using Machine Learning and Behavioral Clustering Techniques
screening_reason: Population: electronics engineers, not clearly students
summary_en: Investigates digital dependency among 268 electronics engineering participants using exploratory factor analysis, a supervised pipeline predicting moderate or severe dependency and K-Means clustering yielding five usage personas. Sleep disruption, reduced academic satisfaction and anxiety-mediated impulsivity dominate the dependency profile.

title: IoT-Enabled Wellbeing Analytics for Academic Staff: Linking Work Environment Signals to Job Satisfaction and Leadership Style
screening_reason: Population: academic staff, not students
summary_en: Examines, through a literature review and case studies, the relationship between IoT-sensed workplace environmental data, sedentary behaviour and job satisfaction among academic staff. No original analysis or results are reported.

title: Performance Assessment of Machine Learning Classifiers in Detecting Psychological Impact of Postgraduate Students due to COVID-19
summary_en: Compares machine learning classifiers for detecting the psychological impact of COVID-19 on Malaysian postgraduate students using an online survey dataset from Mendeley (GAD-7 and concerns about research progress, academic delay and daily life). An artificial neural network achieves the highest accuracy (95.45%), with Logistic Regression, linear SVM and Gaussian Process above 90%.

title: VRAIlexia project: Provide customized support to university students with dyslexia using Artificial Intelligence and Virtual Reality
screening_reason: Focus is learning support for dyslexia; mental health only mentioned as a consequence
summary_en: Describes VRAIlexia, a framework combining artificial intelligence and virtual reality to provide personalised digital tools and learning strategies for university students with dyslexia. No data, model or evaluation results are reported.

title: The 8th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA 2022): General Co-Chairs' Message
screening_reason: Conference front matter; not a study
summary_en: General co-chairs' welcome message for the 8th International Conference on Big Data and Information Analytics (BigDIA 2022). It contains no study.

title: Machine Learning Models for Predicting Suicidal Ideation in University Students
best_result: Optimised Logistic Regression and XGBoost (best recall-accuracy trade-off)
summary_en: Predicts suicidal ideation in university students from psychological and demographic data using Logistic Regression, Random Forest, SVM, neural networks and XGBoost with RFECV feature selection and class balancing. Optimised Logistic Regression and XGBoost give the best balance of recall and accuracy; depression, hopelessness, loneliness and neurodivergence diagnosis are key predictors.

title: Machine Learning Approach to Predict Influence of Smoking on Student Life
screening_reason: Focus is the impact of smoking on academic life
summary_en: Examines the impact of smoking on graduate students' academic life using several machine learning algorithms on a collected dataset. KNN and Random Forest both reach 87.93% accuracy; students who smoke tended to have poorer academic results.

title: Sentiment Analysis on Covid-19 Vaccine
screening_reason: Outcome is opinions on COVID-19 vaccination, not mental health
summary_en: Assesses college students' opinions about the COVID-19 vaccine through social network and sentiment analysis with Naive Bayes, SVM and Logistic Regression. The abstract does not describe the dataset or results.

title: Application of Knowledge Mapping in Behavioral Research of ADHD Adolescents Based on Big Data Citespace Analysis
screening_reason: Bibliometric analysis of ADHD adolescent behaviour research; not students' mental health analytics
summary_en: Applies CiteSpace knowledge mapping to the literature on adolescent ADHD behaviour research, analysing publication stages, disciplines, collaboration networks and keywords. The field shows interdisciplinary expansion, international collaboration, refinement and extension.

title: Machine Learning-Based Student Performance Evaluator: Identifying Key Predictors with LIME
screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance
summary_en: Evaluates student academic performance from internal and external factors, including mental health issues, using the Student Performance Dataset 2024 (98,000 samples, 41 features) and five classifiers. Decision Tree reaches 99.999% cross-validation and 100% hold-out accuracy, and LIME identifies the top five predictors.

title: Study on Automatic Recording and Health Promotion System of University Sports Results
screening_reason: Outcome is physical health status, not mental health
summary_en: Develops an automatic sports results recording and health promotion system for college students that uses wearable physiological data and an SVM to classify health risk levels. Simulation experiments report high accuracy and reliability without specific values.

title: Student Stress Level Prediction using Voting Classifier based on Random Forest and XGBoost
best_result: Random Forest + XGBoost Voting Classifier accuracy 80.28%, weighted F1 0.81
summary_en: Predicts student stress levels (low, moderate, high) from 243 survey responses with 31 attributes using a Voting Classifier combining Random Forest and XGBoost, benchmarked against KNN and Naive Bayes. The ensemble achieves 80.28% accuracy and a weighted F1 of 0.81.

title: Machine Learning Framework for Accurate Mental Stress Detection in University Students Using Random Forest Classification
best_result: Random Forest with Word2Vec accuracy 99%, F1 94%
summary_en: Detects mental stress in university students from online forum text posts using Word2Vec features and Random Forest. The model achieves 99% accuracy and 94% F1, outperforming Naive Bayes, KNN, Decision Tree and SVM.

title: Student Engagement Detection in Classroom using Deep CNN-based Learning Approach
screening_reason: Outcome is classroom engagement, not mental health
summary_en: Classifies student engagement in the classroom from images using transfer learning with a CNN and MobileNet on a small custom dataset. The model achieves 93% overall accuracy.

title: The Impact of Smartphones on Student Learning and Communication
screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; no mental health component
summary_en: Predicts student academic performance from survey-based smartphone usage patterns using several classifiers. Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy, and usage patterns are significantly correlated with performance.

title: The Impact of Credits on Student Performance: A Case Study of Sri Lanka
screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance (GPA); no mental health component
summary_en: Examines the effect of credit load on semester GPA of computer science students at a Sri Lankan university using decision trees, Random Forest and SVM. It finds a weak correlation between credit load and academic performance.

title: Explainable Student Stress Prediction using a Neuro-Symbolic Hybrid Learning Framework
summary_en: Proposes a neuro-symbolic framework combining a neural network with rule-based reasoning on academic, behavioural, social and psychological factors to predict student stress. It achieves 93% accuracy, and SHAP and rule-based insights explain stress-related features; the dataset is not described.

title: EMO-Music: Emotion Recognition Based Music Therapy with Deep Learning on Physiological Signals
summary_en: Presents EMO-Music, a smartwatch-based system that recognises users' emotions from physiological signals with deep learning and plays music accordingly to support college students' well-being. Feasibility was evaluated with the SUS scale, but no results are reported.

title: Explainable Prediction of Daily Stress and Sleep Quality from Passive Smartphone Behavioral Sensing: A SHAP-Based Analysis of the StudentLife Dataset
best_result: Linear Regression stress MAE 1.242, R2 0.008; sleep MAE 1.416, R2 0.112
summary_en: Predicts daily stress and sleep quality from passive smartphone sensing in the StudentLife dataset (48 Dartmouth undergraduates over 10 weeks) using Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM and MLP with leave-one-subject-out validation. Linear Regression is competitive and complex models give no consistent advantage; SHAP identifies physical activity ratio and conversation duration as the main stress predictors.

title: Research on the Structural Relationship Between Parent-Child Relationship and the Usage of Smartphone, Academic Procrastination and Self-Esteem Based on Structural Equation Model Under the Background of Big Data
summary_en: Examines, with structural equation modelling on questionnaire data, how the parent-child relationship relates to smartphone reliance, academic procrastination and self-esteem in 475 grade-nine students in Changzhou. A poorer parent-child relationship is associated with greater smartphone reliance and procrastination, while a better one supports self-esteem.

title: Intelligent System based Distributed Internet Architecture
screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; not about mental health
summary_en: Discusses a distributed Internet architecture for multi-agent systems and the development of college physical education teaching with information technology. It does not address mental health.

title: Mining and Modeling Methods of Psychological Behavior Patterns based on Evolutionary Computation
best_result: Training time reduced by 11.2%, 43.3% and 39.1% versus baselines
summary_en: Proposes mining college students' psychological and behavioural patterns by combining genetic algorithm feature selection with a deep neural network optimised by differential evolution. The model reduces training time by 11.2%, 43.3% and 39.1% compared with baselines; the data are not described.

title: Impact of Data Mining Techniques for Detecting the Anxiety Disorders: A Literature Review
screening_reason: General literature review, not specific to students
summary_en: Reviews literature on data mining techniques for diagnosing depression and anxiety, retrieving 29 papers of which 17 were identified as significant works. It concludes that data mining can substantially support diagnosis prediction.

title: Unveiling the Connection: Music Preferences and Mental Health Through Machine Learning Analysis
screening_reason: Population not specified as students
best_result: Random Forest and KNN accuracy up to 85%
summary_en: Models a person's likely mental state (depression, anxiety, OCD, insomnia) from music preferences, comparing five models. Random Forest and KNN reach up to 85% accuracy; exploratory analysis links high depression, OCD and insomnia to Lofi and higher anxiety to Folk and K-pop.

title: An Efficient and Explainable Model for Student Depression Classification using Boosting Algorithms
summary_en: Classifies student depression from real-world survey data on behavioural, academic and lifestyle factors using resampling and boosting algorithms (Gradient Boosting, XGBoost). All models exceed 90% accuracy with XGBoost best, and SHAP highlights gender, age, academic pressure, CGPA and study satisfaction.

title: Ensemble Machine Learning for Anxiety, Depression, and Panic Attack Detection: A Stacking-Based Approach
screening_reason: Population: adults over 18 assessed by a French university, not explicitly students
summary_en: Detects anxiety, depression and panic attacks from numerical responses of 4,184 people over 18 diagnosed by a French university, using SMOTE and a stacking ensemble of Random Forest, SVM, KNN and AdaBoost. The stacking ensemble achieves the highest accuracy compared with individual classifiers.

title: Explainable User-Level Mental Health Detection via Hybrid Behavioral and Semantic Modeling
screening_reason: Population: Reddit users, not students
best_result: XGBoost with HRM + SBERT features F1 0.86, recall 93%
summary_en: Proposes an explainable user-level framework combining human-readable behavioural metrics with Sentence-BERT embeddings and an XGBoost classifier on the University of Maryland Reddit Suicidality Dataset. It achieves F1 up to 0.86 and 93% recall for at-risk users, with SHAP explanations.

title: EduBoost: An Interpretable Grey-Box Model Approach to Identify and Prevent Student Failure and Dropout
screening_reason: Outcome is student failure and dropout, not mental health
best_result: EduBoost 9-11% gains in accuracy, precision, recall and F1 over White-Box baseline (OULAD)
summary_en: Proposes EduBoost, an interpretable grey-box approach combining a voting ensemble of black-box models with a CART white-box model to identify students at risk of failure and dropout, tested on a university course dataset and OULAD. It improves metrics by 9-11% on OULAD and 2-3% on the university dataset over the white-box baseline.

title: Impact of Alcohol Consumption on Academic Performance of High School Students
screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance; alcohol consumption as predictor
summary_en: Analyses how alcohol consumption affects final grades of high school students using public data from Portugal with Python and SAS Viya. Higher drinking is associated with lower grades, while study time and health are associated with better grades; model R2 is modest.

title: Investigation of Different Classifiers for Stress Level Classification using PCA-Based Machine Learning Method
summary_en: Classifies stress levels in undergraduate students from EEG data, comparing raw preprocessed and PCA-reduced features with KNN, Naive Bayes and MLP. KNN achieves the highest mean accuracy (99%), versus about 50% for Naive Bayes and 80% for MLP.

title: Analysis of Anxiety and Depression in Gaming Individuals
summary_en: Predicts anxiety and depression in people who play games using survey data mainly from students plus some working professionals and several machine learning models. KNN achieves the highest accuracy.

title: Evaluation of University Teachers' Job Burnout Using Neural Networks: A General Framework with Application to Educational Settings
screening_reason: Population: university teachers, not students
summary_en: Models job burnout among college teachers with a multilayer perceptron on the Kaggle 'Are Your Employees Burning Out?' dataset. The model reaches 0.98 accuracy and 0.965 F1.

title: Stress Prediction Among University Students Using Swarm Intelligence and Explainable AI
summary_en: Predicts stress levels in 2,028 Bangladeshi university students from PSS-10 items selected with PCA and information gain, using Logistic Regression tuned by Artificial Bee Colony optimisation. It achieves 98.99% accuracy and 99.01% F1, and LIME shows stress frequency, coping difficulty and perceived loss of control as main drivers.

title: Predicting Daily Depression Scores Using Passive Sensing: A Behaviour-Aware Approach to Missing Value Handling
summary_en: Predicts daily depression scores from longitudinal mobile sensing data of college students over three academic years, using interpolated weekly PHQ-4 labels and a sensor-aware missing-value preprocessing pipeline with regression models. The sensor-aware approach improves performance over standard preprocessing, without reported metrics.

title: EEG-Based Multi-Level Stress Screening Using Machine Learning
summary_en: Classifies multi-level stress in university students (grouped by PSS-10) from EEG signals segmented into 1-5 second intervals with eight time and frequency features and a Bagged Trees classifier. It reports potential for non-invasive stress monitoring without quantitative results.

title: Cloud Enabled Hybrid Machine Learning IoMT Model for Real Time Anxiety Disorder Assessment Using GAD-7, PHQ-9, and UCLA-8 Psychological Scales
screening_reason: Population not specified as students
summary_en: Develops a cloud-based IoMT system to predict anxiety levels and stages from GAD-7, PHQ-9 and UCLA-8 survey data with demographic factors submitted via a mobile app, comparing several machine learning algorithms. Logistic Regression and LDA achieve 97% accuracy, SVM 95% and CatBoost 94%.

title: Symptobot: An AI Diagnostic Website Enhancing Psychological First Aid & Psychiatric Collection and Analysis of Symptoms
summary_en: Presents SymptoBot, an AI diagnostic website for students of the Polytechnic University of the Philippines integrating PHQ-9 depression screening and an AI chatbot providing psychological first aid. Experimental interactions confirmed accurate and natural responses, without quantitative results.

title: Towards Privacy-Preserving Depression Detection: Experiments on Passive Sensor Signal Data
best_result: Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression (near-perfect performance with selected sensor combinations)
summary_en: Explores privacy-preserving depression detection using only non-PII smartphone sensor data from the StudentLife dataset (48 students, 65 days) with prevailing machine learning models. Decision Tree, Gradient Boosting and Logistic Regression perform best, and combinations such as surrounding conversation and phone lock frequency yield near-perfect performance.

title: Role of Artificial Intelligence and Robotics in Shaping the Students: A Higher Educational Perspective
screening_reason: Incoherent abstract; main focus is AI and robotics in higher education
summary_en: Discusses the role of AI and robotics in higher education and examines factors associated with mental health issues among 210 undergraduate students from Delhi NCR and abroad after COVID-19 using SVM, Naive Bayes and Random Forest with 5-fold cross-validation. The abstract is incoherent and reports no quantitative results.

title: A Photoplethysmography (PPG) Sensor based Stress Level Monitoring System for Undergraduate Students of Technical Education
summary_en: Detects stress levels in undergraduate students (aged 17-23) of Indian technical institutions from PPG-derived heart rate data collected with a Polar OH1+ armband. A classification model on the extracted features achieves over 86% accuracy.

title: Machine Learning-Based Detection of Students’ Mental Stress: An In-Depth Analytical Study
summary_en: Classifies student stress into three categories from 24 features gathered from various studies and data sources, including PHQ-9, using chi-squared SelectKBest feature selection and eight supervised algorithms. SVM achieves the highest accuracy (87.3%), and most students fall into mild stress.

title: Optimized Hybrid Stacking Approach for Depression Detection in College Students
best_result: Stacking (SVM, RF, GB with XGBoost meta-classifier) accuracy 91.16%, ROC-AUC 96.60
summary_en: Proposes a stacking ensemble with SVM, Random Forest and Gradient Boosting as base estimators and XGBoost as final classifier for depression detection in college students, using stratified k-fold cross-validation on a balanced dataset. It achieves 91.16% accuracy, 0.913 F1 and 96.60 ROC-AUC; the dataset is not described.

title: Application of Cloud Computing and Speech Recognition Technology in University Golf Smart Guidance
screening_reason: Not about mental health; golf teaching curriculum
summary_en: Introduces the use of cloud computing and speech recognition for golf teaching and curriculum design in undergraduate colleges. It reports a 7.6% increase in guidance efficiency.

title: Predicting Depression and Mental Illness Using Machine Learning Algorithms
best_result: SVM and Random Forest best on dataset 1; Decision Tree best on dataset 2
summary_en: Predicts depression and mental illness using Random Forest, Decision Tree, SVM, KNN and Naive Bayes with SMOTE and grid search on a Kaggle dataset and a survey collected at six Indian universities. SVM and Random Forest perform best on the first dataset and Decision Tree on the second.

title: Enabling University Mental Health Monitoring Through 6G Edge-Cloud IoT Environmental Perception Frameworks
screening_reason: Focus is network architecture; mental health outcomes are not modelled
summary_en: Proposes a standardised 6G edge-cloud IoT framework with federated learning for continuous environmental perception and mental health monitoring on university campuses. Benchmarking shows advantages in latency, energy efficiency, scalability and privacy over cloud-only and edge-only designs, without mental health results.

title: Recommender System for Predicting Students' Academic performance in association with Cognitive state and Affective state using Sentiment Analysis and Association Rule Mining on the closed ended questionnaire
screening_reason: Main focus is academic performance and personality recommendation
summary_en: Proposes a recommender system that uses polarity-based sentiment analysis and association rule mining on closed-ended questionnaires (emotional intelligence, personality, self-esteem, PANAS, Oxford Happiness) to predict student personality with emotions. No evaluation results are reported.

title: Harnessing Machine Learning for Mental Health: A Study on Classifying Depression-Related Social Media Posts
screening_reason: Population: social media users, not students
summary_en: Classifies depression-related social media posts and comments from about 6,500 entries (including Facebook) annotated by undergraduate students, using TF-IDF features and eight classifiers. Gradient Boosting performs best with about 98.5% accuracy.

title: Face Recognition Application with Deep Neural Networks for Teacher Wellbeing Assessment
screening_reason: Population: teachers, not students
summary_en: Develops a face recognition application based on deep neural networks for teacher well-being self-assessment using the Neuroresearch method. No quantitative results are reported.

title: A Review on the analysis of Behavioral pattern of Students during pandemic COVID-19
screening_reason: No explicit data analytics or machine learning method described
summary_en: Reviews prior work on analysing students' behavioural patterns and learning curves during COVID-19 to identify psychologically disturbed students. The abstract does not describe the review method or findings.

title: Revolutionalize Your Learning Experience with EQU ACCESS

summary_en: Presents EQU ACCESS, an online education approach combining behavioural expression analysis, an emotional support chatbot, voice stress detection and visual content description to support students' emotional well-being. It reports 90% accuracy for voice-based anxiety detection, 85% for the chatbot and a 30% rise in perceived emotional support; the data are not described.

title: Student Depression Prediction: A Multimodal Machine Learning Approach
summary_en: Estimates depression in 820 university students by fusing behavioural (mobility, smartphone use, sleep) and linguistic features (essays, social media posts) with PHQ-9 labels, comparing BERT, RoBERTa, Random Forest, Logistic Regression and a fusion ensemble. The fusion ensemble outperforms unimodal baselines with 86% accuracy, and SHAP identifies the most influential predictors.

title: Effective Connectivity of EEG Signals in Diagnosing Alcohol Use Disorder: A Machine Learning Approach
screening_reason: Population: AUD patients and controls, not students
summary_en: Detects alcohol use disorder from EEG effective connectivity (DTF and PDC) in 30 patients and 30 healthy controls using a machine learning model. PDC features achieve higher accuracy (94.5%) than DTF (89.8%).

title: Design and Implementation of a Platform for Managing Stress and Anxiety in Higher Education Based on Wearable Devices*
summary_en: Proposes a digital twin platform for stress management in higher education integrating wearable physiological data (heart rate, HRV, activity, sleep), self-reports and academic context with machine learning to predict individual stress and personalise interventions. Initial results suggest that combining biosignals with academic data improves stress prediction, without reported metrics.

title: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Preventing and Detecting Addiction in Digital Healthcare and social media among students of age group 12 to 18
summary_en: Reviews applications of artificial intelligence and machine learning for detecting and preventing social media addiction and related mental distress among students aged 12 to 18. The abstract does not describe the review method or number of studies.

title: Mental Health Prediction Using Ensemble Learning Approaches with Rebalancing Technique
best_result: Gradient Boosting accuracy 83.8% (anxiety, depression); Random Forest 77.3% (stress)
summary_en: Classifies five severity levels of anxiety, depression and stress in university students from personal information and mental health survey responses using Gradient Boosting, Random Forest and KNN stacking with rebalancing. Gradient Boosting reaches 83.8% accuracy for anxiety and depression and Random Forest 77.3% for stress.

title: Mental Health Stigma: Strategies for Destigmatization in Healthcare Settings
screening_reason: Not data analytics or machine learning; review of stigma interventions
summary_en: Reviews 8-10 papers on causes of mental illness stigma in healthcare settings and strategies to reduce it. RESHAPE, KAP and IBH interventions are reported as effective.

title: Enhancing Academic Performance Prediction Using Feature Transformation and Machine Learning Models
screening_reason: Main outcome is academic performance
best_result: Instance-based methods accuracy gain over 14 percentage points with interaction features
summary_en: Tests whether interaction features built from study hours, sleep, social media use and mental health status improve academic performance prediction on a simulated dataset of 1,000 students with nine Weka classifiers. Interaction terms raise instance-based model accuracy by over 14 percentage points and modestly improve ensembles.

title: Comparative Analysis of Supervised Machine Learning Techniques for Predicting Student Academic Performance
screening_reason: Outcome is academic performance; no mental health component
summary_en: Compares ten supervised algorithms for predicting student pass/fail and multi-class academic performance. Logistic Regression achieves 93.4% in the binary case, while ensemble and boosting models perform well in the multi-class setup.

title: Exploring the Relationship Between Gameplay Log Data and Depression & Anxiety
summary_en: Examines the relationship between gameplay log data from custom shooter and memory games and depression and anxiety in 56 university students using correlation, linear regression, Kolmogorov-Smirnov, ANOVA and Mann-Whitney U tests. Several in-game behaviours, log size, tutorial skipping, age and help-seeking are significantly related to depression and anxiety.

title: SUTD campusX: An Institutional Digital Transformation Approach to Higher Education
screening_reason: Not about mental health analytics; institutional digital transformation
summary_en: Reflection paper describing the campusX digital transformation initiative at the Singapore University of Technology and Design for cyber-physical learning. It does not analyse mental health data.

title: Analyzing the Impact of Facebook Addiction on Academic Performance Using Machine Learning Techniques
screening_reason: Population: Facebook users, not explicitly students; outcome includes academic performance
summary_en: Analyses Facebook addiction and its effects on academic work from a Google Forms survey of 2,222 Bangladeshi Facebook users, testing several machine learning models. Gradient Boosting achieves the best prediction (94.5%), and higher usage is associated with addictive behaviour and reduced academic concentration.

title: Machine Learning Based Depression Prediction: Comparative Analysis of Models and Stacked Ensemble Approach
best_result: Stacking ensemble (SVM, KNN, LR with neural network meta-model) accuracy 96.36%
summary_en: Predicts depression from a Google survey of 550 university students using Logistic Regression, SVM, KNN, Decision Tree and neural networks. The neural network reaches 94.55%, and a stacking ensemble with a neural network meta-model achieves 96.36% accuracy.

title: Learnease AI: A Multimodal Deep Learning and Computer Vision Framework for Real-Time Emotion and Stress Pattern Recognition in Academic Environments
summary_en: Proposes Learnease AI, a Django web tool that identifies student emotions and stress levels from facial images (OpenCV), survey answers and behavioural patterns using machine learning, with a dashboard for personalised feedback. It reports high detection accuracy without specific metrics or data description.

title: Early Detection of Mental and Behavioral Health Issues from High-School Academic Performance
summary_en: Applies unsupervised clustering to academic performance data of over 500 students in mid-sized Illinois high schools to classify them as stable, monitor or critical for early detection of mental and behavioural health issues. Cluster sizes are compared with CDC and NAMI adolescent mental health statistics, but no results are reported.

title: Design and Application of a Student Physical Health Monitoring and Management System Based on Optimized Learning Algorithm
screening_reason: Outcome is physical health, not mental health
summary_en: Proposes an ant-lion-optimised Bi-LSTM (OP_LSTM) for monitoring students' physical health on Kaggle's Student Physical Health dataset. It achieves 0.97 accuracy and 0.97 F1, outperforming existing approaches.

title: Evaluation of Machine Learning Algorithms for Detecting Student Stress Levels
summary_en: Evaluates seven machine learning and four deep learning models with SMOTE and GridSearchCV for classifying stress levels in a secondary PSS-10 dataset of 2,028 university students. Logistic Regression achieves the highest accuracy (99.75%), followed by SVM (99.50% with SMOTE).

title: The correction system of student actions in the physical education classroom based on improved machine learning
screening_reason: Not about mental health; physical education action correction
summary_en: Proposes a Hidden Markov Model-assisted correction system to improve student behaviour in university physical education classes. Simulations report a 98.8% predictive rate and 96.8% efficiency.

title: CNNs for Anxiety Risk Classification and Prediction in Mental Health
summary_en: Classifies college students' anxiety into severity levels with a convolutional neural network. The model achieves 98% accuracy and an MSE of 0.02; the dataset is not described.

title: Performance Comparison of Machine Learning Algorithms for Depression Risk Prediction using PHQ-9 Questionnaire
best_result: Random Forest accuracy 75.91% (severity classification); Gradient Boosting R2 0.522, MAE 4.04 (score regression)
summary_en: Compares machine learning algorithms for classifying PHQ-9 depression severity and for regressing PHQ-9 scores from non-PHQ psychosocial features in university students. Random Forest performs best in classification (75.91%) and Gradient Boosting in regression (R2 0.522, MAE 4.04).

title: Objectives, Methods, and Challenges of Applying Intelligent Assessment in Education: A systematic review
screening_reason: Mental health is only one of several assessment objectives reviewed
summary_en: Systematic review of 51 studies (2015-2024) on intelligent assessment in education, grouping objectives into competence and knowledge, personality and mental health, and teaching and learning processes. title: AI-Driven Integration of Ayurveda and Yoga for Mental Health Support in Students and Working Professionals: A Comprehensive Framework
screening_reason: Conceptual review; population includes working professionals
summary_en: Reviews literature and proposes a conceptual framework integrating AI with Ayurveda and yoga to provide personalised mental health interventions for students and working professionals based on physiological, psychological and lifestyle data. No empirical data or results are reported.

title: The Impact of Emotion Re-Categorization on Deep Learning Models for Text-Based Emotion Classification: A Case Study with the ISEAR Dataset
screening_reason: Population: not students; general emotion text dataset
summary_en: Evaluates the effect of re-categorising ISEAR emotions from seven to five classes on CNN, LSTM, BiLSTM and GRU text classifiers for mental health chatbots. CNN reaches 76.4% with five classes versus 61.1% with seven, and deployment in a chatbot in Ghana obtained 65% satisfaction in cultural sensitivity.

title: Multi-model Real-Time Physiological Data Analysis for Student Concentration Monitoring
screening_reason: Main outcome is concentration and cognitive state
summary_en: Develops a system that classifies student concentration and mental fatigue from EEG, HRV and GSR signals using signal processing and machine learning models. It reports a validated system without quantitative results.

title: AI-Enhanced Counseling for Undergraduates: A Novel Application of Machine Learning for Personality Matching and Stress Assessment
summary_en: Designs an AI-enhanced university counselling solution with rule-based counsellor-student personality matching and machine learning stress assessment, evaluated with survey data from 98 Sri Lankan university students. Random Forest achieves 95.2% accuracy in stress prediction, with study hours, sleep and physical activity as key features, and 80% of students expressed interest.

title: Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) Performance in Behavior-Based of Self-Esteem Level Prediction
summary_en: Pilot study predicting self-esteem levels in 47 university students from behaviour-based questionnaire data using an Extreme Learning Machine with ten-fold cross-validation and different activation functions. The best accuracy is 74.5% with ReLU and 16 hidden neurons.

title: Using Admission Records and Student Survey Responses for Early Prediction of CS1 Performance
screening_reason: Outcome is course academic performance, not mental health
summary_en: Predicts at-risk performance in the first programming course (CS1) from admissions records and pre-course survey data using several model families, testing on the Fall 2024 cohort. XGBoost performs best (F2 0.71, 81% of at-risk students identified), and SHAP highlights AP scores, calculus background and GPA.

title: FEdRank: Federated Learning for Collaborative Institutional Ranking based on Student Performance
screening_reason: Outcome is institutional ranking by academic performance, not mental health
summary_en: Proposes FEdRank, a federated learning framework enabling universities to collaboratively train models on academic performance metrics such as CGPA and placements to rank institutions with Borda count. It reports stable convergence and accuracy across institutions without specific values.

title: Mental Health Detection Using Late Fusion Transformer Models With Llm Chat Integration
screening_reason: Population not specified as students
best_result: DistilBERT + XLM-RoBERTa late fusion accuracy 76.68%; weighted F1 76.54%
